trans-unit.source: Some installed extensions can be enabled in the Agents window.

Extensions that could be useful in the Agents window and don't rely on views, debugging, or other features that it doesn't have are enabled automatically instead. You can disable them like any other extension.

Extensions that support the Agents window are listed under Supported and are enabled by default. Other extensions are listed under Other Extensions and are disabled by default because they might not work as expected.

Use the search box to filter extensions by name, identifier, publisher, or description. Press Tab to move to the list, use the Up and Down Arrow keys to move between extensions, and press Space or Enter to enable or disable the focused extension. Use the Left and Right Arrow keys on a group to collapse or expand it.

You are in the Extensions section of Agent Customizations. It lists the extensions installed in VS Code and whether each one runs in the Agents window. Enabling or disabling an extension here only affects the Agents window.

When a change requires restarting extensions or reloading the window, the extension is marked as requiring a restart and a Restart Extensions or Reload Window button appears next to the section title.

Extensions listed under Suggested haven't declared support for the Agents window but could be useful there, for example because they add tools, MCP servers, or syntax highlighting. Like other extensions, they are disabled by default.

Choose which installed extensions run in the Agents window. Extensions that haven't declared support for the Agents window are disabled by default and might not work as expected. Changes only apply to the Agents window.

Choose which installed extensions run in the Agents window. Extensions that haven't declared support for the Agents window might not work as expected. They are disabled by default, unless they could be useful there and don't rely on features that the Agents window doesn't have. Changes only apply to the Agents window.

Extensions

When enabled, installed extensions that haven't declared support for the Agents window are enabled there automatically when they could be useful, such as extensions that add tools, MCP servers, or syntax highlighting, and don't rely on views, debugging, or other features that the Agents window doesn't have. You can still disable them from the Extensions section of Agent Customizations. Requires `#{0}#`.

When enabled, you can choose which installed extensions run in the Agents window from the Extensions section of Agent Customizations. When disabled, extensions that don't support the Agents window stay disabled there, and your previous choices are kept but ignored.

When enabled, the Agents window suggests installed extensions that could be useful there, such as extensions that add tools, MCP servers, or syntax highlighting. The Extensions section of Agent Customizations lists them in a Suggested group, and its entry point shows a badge while they are disabled, until you open the section. Requires `#{0}#`.
When enabled, non-built-in extensions can declare whether they support running in the Agents window. Built-in extensions can declare support without enabling this setting.
